sentences.text:
(Presently Lodged In Distt. Jail Bhilwara)
 ----Petitioner  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2.

Rampali Devi W/o Ram Kishan Mali, Badanpura, P.s.
 Pander, Distt. Shahpura.
----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. S.K. Bhati For Respondent(s) : Mr. Urja Ram Kalbi, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 12/11/2024 1.

This application for bail under Section 483 of BNSS has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.145/2023, registered at Police Station Pander, District Shahpura, for offences under Sections 376(2)(n) & 376(3) of IPC; Sections 5(l)/6 & 11(iv)/12 of POCSO Act; Sections 67 & 67-B of Information Technology Act.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner who is aged about 18 years is in judicial custody since 23.09.2023.

Learned counsel submitted that the allegations against the present petitioner is that in the month of August, 2023 the petitioner committed sexual assault- Rape upon victim 'G' and [2024:RJ-JD:45618] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-9587/2024] also captured her obscene photographs and videos and circulated them on social media platform.

Learned counsel submitted that the case file prima facie indicates that the petitioner and victim 'G' were having Pinkesh vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45618) on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102261380/
1 affair, however, on turning relations between them sour, the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Learned counsel further contended that the statements of the victim 'G' have been recorded before the competent Criminal Court on 10.07.2024 as PW-1 and, therefore, now there is no apprehension of the petitioner influencing her or tampering with the evidence.
4. Lastly, learned counsel contended that the statements of the victim 'G' have already been recorded; the trial against the petitioner is likely to consume sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioner.
5.
Per Contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail application.

6. Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that the petitioner who is aged about 18 years is in judicial custody since 23.09.2023; the petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents; the statements of victim 'G' have already been recorded before the competent Criminal Court and the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the remaining prosecution witnesses or fleeing away from justice, in case he is enlarged on bail, thus without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioners on bail.
Consequently, the second bail application under Section 483 of BNSS is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Pinkesh S/o Chouthmal arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.145/2023,
registered at Police Station Pander, District Shahpura, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/-
each, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court, for his appearance before that Court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 36-mohit/-
